summary: Midday mini-burst leads to asymmetric GPU attach failures and tenant unfairness in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: During a customer-reported midday spike (11:45-12:05 PDT) DataFlux observed sustained p50/p95 latency increases and a 20-30% throughput loss on their Dedicated pool routes. The symptom set includes frequent GPU attach failures (attach retries 5-10x baseline) for some internal allocator workers and concurrent over-allocation on others, producing asymmetric tenant fairness where some DataFlux shards consumed >60% of available slots for short windows.

Impact: Customer-facing inference throughput dropped ~25% for 22 minutes, p95 latency increased from 140ms to 420ms for batch routes. No user-visible 5xx surfaced to the customer API, but many requests experienced attach backoff and subsequent queueing. Customer is on Dedicated plan with strict performance requirements.

Environment: prod-us-west-2, dedicated pool pool-DFX-west-42, serving-runtime v2.6.1, autoscaler v1.9.0, scheduler v3.2. Deployed model variants: open/llama-2-13b-8k (quantized), redwood/opt-6.7b.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Normal traffic with 6-10 long-lived streams per tenant.
2) At ~11:45 PDT DataFlux scheduling shows a series of many short-lived parallel connections (mini-burst) from 6 internal shards hitting warmup-prefetch paths.
3) Allocator logs show a spike in attach attempts; some attach calls fail with transient timeouts and then backoff.
4) Meanwhile other allocator workers succeed and hold slots, producing asymmetric slot distribution.
5) Autoscaler did not spin additional GPUs within the burst window due to attach failures and conservative scaling cooldown, leading to queueing.

Observed behavior: GPU attach failures (timeout, code ATTACH_TIMEOUT) followed by worker-level retries; heterogeneous slot retention across workers; autoscaler telemetry shows attach_rollback spikes; grafana panels: pool-attach-overview (panel id 71), slot-occupancy-heatmap (panel id 29) show skew. Kibana query used: "service:allocator AND pool:pool-DFX-west-42 AND message:/ATTACH_TIMEOUT/".

Expected behavior: Attach attempts should succeed or autoscaler should add capacity gracefully; slot allocation should remain balanced across allocator workers to avoid short windows of unfairness.

Attachments: snippets from allocator logs, Grafana screenshots, Kibana links, customer request ID logs attached in comments.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: mini-burst of short-lived prefetch/warmup connections caused many concurrent attach attempts which triggered a combination of (a) allocator attach contention (b) transient nvlink/driver hiccup on a subset of nodes, and (c) autoscaler cooldown preventing additional GPU attachments. Evidence: allocator logs show repeated ATTACH_TIMEOUT messages correlated with increased ephemeral-connection-rate metric. Node diagnostics for nodes gpunode-45..48 show elevated driver attach latencies on two nodes. No kernel crashes or OOMs observed.

What we tried: 1) Forced a soft-eviction of long-held idle slots to rebalance (mitigation) 2) Temporarily lowered autoscaler cooldown and triggered a scale-up (manual) which recovered capacity after ~3 minutes 3) Patched allocator to add additional jitter to attach attempts in a test branch (see PR).

Partial findings: Rebalancing reduced the asymmetric slot hogging but did not eliminate attach timeouts. Manual scale-up restored throughput but was delayed by attach retries; root cause appears to be subtle attach stall on a small subset of GPU hosts combined with high attach concurrency.

resolution:
Temporary mitigation: manual scale-up and targeted soft-eviction of idle slots restored balance and throughput. Applied a temporary autoscaler cooldown override for the affected pool to allow faster scale-up during bursts. A small runtime patch (attach jitter) was deployed to the staging cluster to reduce synchronized attach retries.

Permanent fix planned: change attach backoff/jitter algorithm, add attach success rate monitoring and autoscaler probes that consider attach_failure_ratio before deciding not to scale. See follow-up actions.
root_cause: Combination of a high-concurrency short-lived connection burst from the customer (mini-burst) that led to synchronized attach retries and transient attach stalls on a small subset of GPU hosts. The autoscaler's cooldown behavior and lack of attach-failure-aware probes prevented rapid additional capacity, resulting in asymmetric slot retention (noisy-tenant effect) and throughput loss.
